geometry_edits.rationale: Increase the bar bend so the massing has a clearer dominant gesture and sectional continuity.
Align the courtyard opening to the verified access side to strengthen the public threshold.
Widen the carve so it behaves more like a usable neighborhood court.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the dominant bent gesture and make the bar read as a more continuous spatial sequence rather than a shallow kink.
Increase sectional/plan emphasis so the main mass has a clearer hierarchy and more visible circulation potential.
Keep the public carve aligned to the verified access side so the courtyard becomes a legible street-facing threshold.
Enlarge the void slightly to make it read as usable public space rather than a narrow decorative bite.

rationale: The candidate reads as a bent bar with a courtyard carve, so it has a recognizable dominant idea and some alignment with the neighborhood-living brief: compact mass, one void, and an attempt at public threshold. However, the silhouette is only moderately coherent across the four views because the bent mass and the inner subtraction are not yet fully unified into one continuous spatial rule. More importantly, the section does not convincingly support the program contract: the mass stays low and thin, with no clear evidence of a robust active ground threshold or a calm upper hierarchy for five floors of neighborhood living. The open-space figure is present but still feels like a generic subtraction rather than a truly usable public court/terrace tied to the access edge. Repair integrity is strong because the geometry appears manifold and not over-clipped, but program appropriateness and section-program fit remain below passing due to the weak relationship between mass, ground, and section.
